evidence.text: The reported quarter was pre-guided and the bar has come down. On 2026-08-06 the CFO said Q3 CELSIUS brand should 'look a lot like the second' (Q2: -11.7% y/y to about $387M) and gross margin should stay in the high 40s. Since then Chartmill shows the Q3 revenue estimate cut 7.57% in three months, and JPMorgan, UBS and TD Cowen cut targets. Bottom-up arithmetic (CELSIUS about -12% on Q3 2025's ~$393M, plus Alani Nu about +20% on $332.0M, plus Rockstar about $66M) gives roughly $810M, inside the $800-816M bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue missed $870-886M consensus by about 6% and the stock fell 18.46%. Q3 2025 beat revenue ($725.1M vs $715.7M) and EPS ($0.42 vs $0.27) and still fell 24.8% on the Q4 'noise' warning. This name has not paid for the reported quarter when the forward read is soft.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The pre-guide is public and the bar has been cut to it, which is why this is sized near zero. If the market expected a further CELSIUS miss, the bar would sit below $795M and the skew would be put-bid; instead it is $800-816M and upside is paid.
evidence.independence: Consensus revision: https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CELH/estimates. Q3 2025 brand dollars: https://ir.celsiusholdingsinc.com/news/news-details/2025/Celsius-Holdings-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx. Target cuts: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/celh/. Shares the Q2 transcript with the diesel finding (different passages).

evidence.text: Alani Nu consumption ran ahead into Q3. Management said Alani scans were about +50% after the Witch's Brew launch (Barclays, 2026-09-08; Witch's Brew billed on Aug 6 as 'the largest limited-time offer in the brand's history'). PepsiCo's Q3 prepared remarks (2026-10-08, 12 weeks to Sept 5) say 'the partnership with Celsius Holdings gained value share and holds nearly 20 percent share of the category'. Q2 Alani reported net sales grew +21% against +56% scans. If the Q3 gross-to-net gap narrows now the Pepsi DSD transition is complete, Alani could print above the roughly +20% (about $400M) implied in the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Alani +21% reported was not enough to offset CELSIUS -12%, and the stock fell 18.46%. Q1 2026 (+4.45%) and Q4 2025 (+6.94%) were Alani-led beats bought modestly. On this name Alani strength buys single digits; CELSIUS weakness costs double digits.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The +50% scan figure was public on Sept 8, and the stock fell 6.5% that day on the CELSIUS read, not on Alani. PepsiCo's share statement came after Celsius last spoke, and the consensus cut of 7.6% over three months suggests models did not lift Alani. If it were priced, estimates would have risen since August, not fallen. Capped small because the revenue bar is disputed by about $15M and 'nearly 20 percent' is flat against Q2's 20.1%.
evidence.independence: Barclays scan figures via B. Riley's preview: https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/briley-reiterates-buy-on-celsius-stock-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4921046. Q2 Alani +56% scans and the Witch's Brew LTO: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/celsius-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-06/. Net of the rest: CELSIUS (about 45% of sales) is guided down about 12%, so Alani has to carry the print.

evidence.text: CELSIUS brand consumption got worse after the Q2 call. At Barclays on 2026-09-08 management put CELSIUS scans at -5% to -10% (IRI), against -2% tracked retail sales in Q2 that the CFO had called 'the consumer'. That undercuts the Aug 6 claim that the brand 'exit[s] the year back into growth', which matters for Q4/2027 commentary on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The forward read on CELSIUS drove the last two big moves: -24.8% on 2025-11-06 (Q4 noise warning) and -18.46% on 2026-08-06 (brand -12%, 'went too deep' on rationalization). The stock also fell 6.5% on 2026-09-09, the day after these scan figures.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell 6.5% on it in September. But the stock is now up 13% from the Sept 9 close of $27.64, so the rebound has run ahead of any evidence that scans have turned. If the market still held the September read, the stock would not have rallied 11.8% in five sessions into the print with upside skew.
evidence.independence: The same Barclays figure is cited independently in B. Riley's 2026-11-02 preview: https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/briley-reiterates-buy-on-celsius-stock-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4921046. That is one event in two write-ups, so it counts once. Shrunk for 5.5 days to cover of short interest.

evidence.text: Diesel rose well above the level the margin guide was set at. The Aug 6 high-40s gross margin guide was explicitly 'at current diesel and aluminum levels', with improvement only 'if fuel or aluminum moderates'. EIA on-highway diesel was $5.348 the week of Aug 3, $5.652 on Aug 24 and $5.967 on Sept 7 (+11.6% from the guide date), with secondary reports of a record about $6.53 the week of Sept 21. B. Riley's preview notes fuel costs rose in August and September. That pressures Q3 gross margin below Q2's 48.1% and the Q4 margin commentary.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin compression was part of the Q2 miss (48.1% vs 51.5%, adjusted EBITDA -12%), and the stock fell 18.46%. Q3 2025 at 51.3% margin was overshadowed by the Q4 warning.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. B. Riley models a 21.1% EBITDA margin against 22.5% in Q2, and a Morgan Stanley H2 EBITDA cut on fuel is listed in late September on stockanalysis. If fully priced, EPS consensus would sit below Q2's $0.36; it is $0.35-0.36. The transmission from diesel to COGS is a proxy: outbound freight is a mid-single-digit share of sales, so this is likely tens of basis points. Sized small.
evidence.independence: Aug 3 baseline: https://www.agrinews-pubs.com/community-contributed/2026/08/04/fuel-gauge-for-week-ending-aug-3/. Fuel costs flagged in B. Riley's preview: https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/briley-reiterates-buy-on-celsius-stock-ahead-of-q3-results-93CH-4921046. The guide's diesel condition is in the Q2 transcript, page 7 (same document as finding 1).

evidence.text: New forward information is promised for this call. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Forward commentary has moved this stock the most: -24.8% (Q4 noise, Nov 2025), +6.94% (Feb 2026, the 2026 setup), -18.46% (Aug 2026, Q3 'like Q2').
evidence.why_not_priced: The content is unknown until the call, so only its existence is priced, mainly through the implied move. Positive lean because retailers were said to be 'leaning in on 2027 planning earlier than they ever had' and the company controls what it discloses.
evidence.independence: Q2 transcript page 8 (16-ounce offering in '27): https://s203.q4cdn.com/427437840/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Celsius-Holdings-Second-Quarter-2026-Earnings-Conference-Call-Transcript.pdf. evidence.text: Figma has beaten the midpoint of its own revenue guide by about 5.5-6% in each of the last two quarters. Q1 2026 came in at $333.4M against a $315-317M guide (+5.5%), Q2 at $370.1M against $348-350M (+6.0%), and Q4 2025 at $303.8M was above its range. The Q3 guide of $373-375M implies only about 1% sequential growth, against 11% from Q1 to Q2. On the call the CFO called it a 'snapshot' that excludes beta products, which he labelled upside. Repeating the pattern would give about $390-397M, 3-5% above the about $377M consensus, which sits only about 1% above the guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, a 5.5% beat over the guide midpoint plus a $55M FY raise, closed +13.24% (2026-05-14). Q2 2026, a 6.0% beat plus a $40M FY raise, closed -14.85% (2026-08-05) on AI cost of revenue (+117%) and the soft Q3 sequential guide. A revenue beat by itself has not set the sign on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $376.6-379.7M sits only 0.7-1.5% above the guide midpoint, while the last two quarters beat by about 6%. If the sell-side had priced the pattern, consensus would be near $390M. The buy side probably expects a beat, which is why this is sized small and not at the implied move.
evidence.independence: Q1 actual vs guide from a different document: Q4 2025 release (Q1 guide $315-317M, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1579878/000162828026009024/fy25pressrelease.htm) and Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579878/000162828026035087/q126pressrelease.htm). CFO's 'beta excluded = upside' comment from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15392832623961088).

evidence.text: On 2026-08-25, partway through Q3, Figma gave 2x more AI credits on Professional and 1.6x on Organization/Enterprise add-ons at an unchanged price. The pay-as-you-go spending cap also stayed the same, so it now buys more usage. That is an effective per-credit price cut of about 50% and 37.5%. The CFO had said on 08-05 that most AI revenue comes through coterminous add-ons and warned a shift to pay-as-you-go would add variability. This lowers the AI-credit expansion and overage revenue per unit of usage for 5 weeks of Q3 and all of the Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: AI monetization has moved the stock before: March 2026 credit-limit enforcement drew a selloff on churn/monetization fears (https://rallies.ai/news/figma-tumbles-as-march-ai-credit-enforcement-revives-churn-and-monetization-concerns). No earnings print has yet isolated AI-credit revenue as a line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The change was posted on a help-centre page and a pricing tracker (https://usagepricing.com/blueprint/activity/figma-2026-08-25-packaging), not in a press release or an 8-K, and no analyst note I found quantifies it. If it were priced, previews would discuss lower AI add-on revenue in the Q4 guide; the Oct PT cuts cite gross margin, not this. Offsetting: it may lift usage and is probably partly in the Aug 5 guide if it was planned.
evidence.independence: Same Figma help page as the agent-GA finding; the pricing tracker reads it as a price cut. Any revenue effect is my inference; the company has not quantified one.

evidence.text: The Figma agent in Design and Weave moved from open beta to general availability on 2026-10-06 and now consumes paid AI credits. The CFO said on 08-05 that beta and early-access products (agent, Make on local code, Motion and others) are excluded from guidance and would be upside once monetized. The Q4 guide given tonight is the first that can include a paid agent.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises were bought in May (+13.24%) and sold in August (-14.85%). In August the sequential Q3 guide was the line cited as a deceleration worry.
evidence.why_not_priced: The GA date appears on a support page, not in a press release, and no preview I found mentions it. If priced, Q4 consensus would sit above a run-rate extension of the Q3 guide. The guidance philosophy ('wait for sustained trends') means management may still keep it out of the Q4 guide, which caps this finding.
evidence.independence: The CFO's statement that beta is excluded from guidance comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15392832623961088). The GA date shares a document with the credit-price-cut finding.

evidence.text: The guide already embeds deep H2 operating-margin compression. FY2026 non-GAAP operating income is guided at $125-135M and was maintained on 08-05. H1 delivered about $89M (Q1 about 16% of $333.4M, about $53M; Q2 $36.1M), so H2 is guided at about $41M on about $762M of revenue, roughly a 5% margin against about 13% in H1. A revenue beat at Figma's usual 85% gross margin clears that bar easily.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's -14.85% was attributed to profit reversal and AI cost (https://www.webull.com/news/15358948900545536). That is the line this name has traded on most recently, so a profit beat matters.
evidence.why_not_priced: The implied H2 figure is arithmetic on the release and is not stated by the company. Q3 consensus EPS of about $0.05 non-GAAP (FXEmpire) is roughly consistent with the compressed guide, so a beat is not in the estimates. Preview commentary (Stifel's cut) focuses on GM falling from 90%+ to mid-80s, not on how low the operating-income bar sits.
evidence.independence: Q1 non-GAAP margin of 16% from a separate summary of the Q1 release (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/figma-q1-2026-earnings-beat-110945684.html). Offset by the next finding (beta inference cost).
